subject: Re: Redwood observability & infra comparison — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood observability & infra comparison — quick recap and next steps

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery + recommended next steps so we all have alignment: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Acme is evaluating inference providers for an internal recommender pilot; main criteria are token-level latency, predictable tail latency, cost per 1M tokens, and out-of-the-box observability (per-route dashboards, trace-level sampling, and usage analytics).
- A few constraints: SOC 2 evidence and KMS integration for keys are required before pilot, and they'd like a short shootout vs the hyperscaler endpoints they currently use.

Redwood differentiators we highlighted:
- Token-level tracing + per-route dashboards so you can map latency and cost to specific prompts/routes.
- Smart routing and fallbacks to keep latency SLOs during spikes.
- Built-in cost controls (batching/quantization suggestions) and rollout policies for predictable economics.

Proposed next steps (suggested timeline):
1) Shared test plan: Redwood sends an observability-focused test plan + short sandbox credentials (we'll provide deterministic load scripts). — Action: Marissa (today) -> attached deck + test plan.
2) Security review: Acme to share SOC2 checklist items we need; we'll loop in security docs. — Action: Acme security.
3) Demo deep-dive: Stephanie to run a 30–45m session focused on tracing, dashboards, and cost breakdown (week of 3/23). — Action: Stephanie / Acme SREs.
4) Pilot kickoff: 2-week pilot running Redwood vs hyperscaler endpoints with matched traffic. Redwood will assign an SE to help analyze traces and dashboards. — Target: start 3/23–3/30.

Attachments: Redwood-Observability-Spotlight.pdf (deck), RWD-observability-test-plan.md (test plan).

If that looks right, can you confirm which week you'd prefer for the demo and the list of people to include from your side?

Thanks,
Marissa

Subject: Re: Redwood observability & infra comparison — quick recap and next steps

Sarah — thanks, adding a short implementation-oriented checklist below (we'll also add to the test plan doc):

Telemetry checklist for shootout (minimal):
- Inject X-Request-ID: unique per user request (recommended)
- Include client-provided correlation_id for cross-service joins
- Forward original request metadata via headers: prompt_id, route_id, model_variant
- Capture token-level timestamps at generation start/end (we can instrument with our SDK or via proxy)
- Error and retry counters; label by route and model_variant

Proposed test metrics (what we'll measure):
- p50/p95/p99 latency per-route and per-model_variant
- Per-token cost and aggregate cost per 1M tokens
- Tail latency under burst (10x baseline qps)
- Percentage of requests hitting fallbacks/variants during capacity constraints
- Observability coverage: sampling rate and span completeness

We will provide: sandbox key, load scripts (k6), and an instrumentation snippet for your infra team to paste into the proxy. Attaching RWD-observability-test-plan.md to this thread.

Stephanie — can you run the live tracing demo and show how we'd map a slow request to a prompt and cost bucket?

Thanks,
Neha
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
